name: TX-25
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Williams running with $1.1M cash on hand
No polls or expert ratings; markets price ~95% Republican
model.rationale: The R+11 district, an incumbent with over $1 million banked, and prediction markets pricing the Republican near 95% all point the same direction, with no evidence of a competitive Democratic campaign. The fundamentals-based margin of roughly -15 fits comfortably.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Sims within single digits, or a surge in Democratic fundraising, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-25 is a solidly Republican district west of Fort Worth, with a partisan lean of about eleven points toward the GOP. Incumbent Roger Williams is running for reelection and holds a clear financial edge, with $1.4 million raised and $1.1 million on hand. Democrat Dione Sims has no reported fundraising and no outside spending has surfaced on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 95%. The expected margin is roughly fifteen points for Williams, with uncertainty wide enough that a shock could tighten things but not plausibly flip the seat.
